title: THE FIRST FRAME
goal: Catch the first thought before it expands into a whole story.

steps.text: A trigger flickers.

title: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
goal: Weigh visible facts on both sides before deciding what they mean.

title: MARGIN AROUND THE LOOP
goal: Give a recurring question a boundary, complete something outside it, and end this round of the loop.

steps.text: Say the repeated question once, exactly as it keeps returning.
Ask how the signal differs from the intention.
Choose the later questions as your restart marker.
Complete one bounded task outside the loop.
End the unfinished mental loop.

win: The question was said once, a later restart marker was chosen, and one bounded task finished outside the loop.
mindBend: A loop can remain unfinished without remaining active. Deliberately storing the restart point lets the brain stop using repetition as memory.
formulaFlow: Voice It → Divide Parts → Hold Later → Take Action → Close Loop

title: KEEP ONE FACT
goal: Make a decision that fits the uncertainty and capacity available, then set a review point.

steps.text: Name what is still uncertain.
Name how much time or capacity you actually have.
Wait one beat before choosing.
Choose the next review spot and stop there.

win: The choice was made after one pause and uncertainty was contained by a specific future review rather than repeated reopening.
mindBend: A review point converts 'What if I'm wrong?' from a permanent alarm into a scheduled information check.

title: CHOICE, NOT COMMAND
goal: Put a chosen priority beside the thought and act on that priority without answering the mental command.

steps.text: Say, “My mind is giving me an instruction.”
Name one priority that exists outside the thought.
Choose one finishable action that serves that priority.
Do the first ten seconds.
Keep the thought unanswered and name where you will resume.

win: The first ten seconds of a priority-based action happened while the thought remained unresolved and non-authoritative.
mindBend: A thought can use command-shaped language without possessing command authority. Behaviour is where authority is actually granted.
